chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave of ours whom I took with me, and I ordered him, so he performed Tamattu' and entered into Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah, and I did not slaughter on his behalf. Is it for him to fast after the departure, and the days mentioned by Allah, Exalted and Mighty, have passed? He said: Why did you not order him to perform the exclusive Hajj? I said: I sought the goodness. He said: Just as you sought the goodness, so slaughter a fat sheep, and that would be on the last day of departure.

key_terms.إِفْرَاد: Ifrad: Performing Hajj exclusively without combining it with Umrah.
key_terms.التَّمَتُّع: Tamattu' Hajj: Performing Umrah first, then Hajj in the same pilgrimage season.
key_terms.النَّفْر: Al-Nafar: The departure from Mina after standing at Arafat.
key_terms.شَاة: Sheep: The animal designated for the sacrificial offering (Hady).
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a master orders his slave to perform Hajj al-Tamattu' but fails to slaughter the sacrifice for him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial liability (damm) of the master when he fails to slaughter the sacrificial animal for a slave performing Hajj al-Tamattu', ruling that the master must provide a fat sheep on the slave's behalf. The Imam’s response, 'As you sought good, so slaughter,' highlights the principle that the master’s intent and action (or inaction) directly determine the ritual validity and compensation for the dependent, linking the master's spiritual intent to the slave's legal status.
